analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md: the Last-updated date (line 3) and one new runtime-constants table row for the watchdog crash-restart timing (hunk at head line 2016). No executable code, protocol, key custody, authorization, or cache-storage logic changes. The supplied units are the pre-existing portions of the file at head lines 397-1270, which the diff does not touch. I read them for context only, and the new watchdog row sits outside them (the head range is truncated at 1270). I checked the described behavior against the threat model and found no new attack surface or invalidated assumption. The logout section (head lines 538-587) matches A-008 and T-053: the credential is sent only to its recorded issuer, there are no redirects, and remote revocation is confirmed only on HTTP 204. The add-on hold section (head lines 910-937) matches TB-012, T-059 and T-060. The prefix-cache slot posture text matches T-041 (no prompt-derived data on disk, KEK-wipe purge). The new watchdog row documents the 1-2 minute crash-restart window and the 300 s grace for crash-loop chains. This relates to T-043 (watchdog rollback authority is the replaceable provider binary) and TB-003 availability. It only documents behavior and does not weaken any control. Remaining limits: I could not verify that WatchdogDecision.swift actually implements the documented values, because the source was not supplied. The documentation claims about platform-side revocation (`/v1/device/revoke`) depend on external platform implementation and are unverified here. No finding is raised.
